extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, students and researchers interested in the 2016 Republican National Convention
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the 2016 Republican National Convention in Cleveland, covering delegate counts, planning, speaker lineup and notable speeches, controversies, security and viewership. The page documents procedural details, timeline and public reception of the convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegate vote recording (RNC rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The delegations of Alaska, District of Columbia and Utah reported votes for other candidates, which were nonetheless recorded by the convention secretary as bound votes for Trump according to RNC rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "The delegations of Alaska, District of Columbia and Utah reported votes for other candidates, which were nonetheless recorded by the convention secretary as bound votes for Trump according to RNC rules." Implies that delegate vote reporting and the official recording are governed by party rules that can bind how votes are entered into the convention record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker selection and endorsement expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Trump sought to bar those who have not endorsed him from addressing the convention, making comments aimed at former primary rivals who have declined to endorse him – Bush, Carly Fiorina, Lindsey Graham and George Pataki.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "Trump sought to bar those who have not endorsed him from addressing the convention..." Demonstrates a selection criterion (endorsement status) the campaign considered when deciding whom to invite to speak, though exceptions occurred (e.g., Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz later appeared on the schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of vice-presidential running mate announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Trump also initially stated that he would announce his vice-presidential running mate at the convention itself, rather than before the convention, but the campaign eventually announced plans to announce a running mate the week before the convention and named Mike Pence on July 15, 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "Trump also initially stated that he would announce his vice-presidential running mate at the convention itself..." and later: "the campaign eventually announced plans to announce a running mate the week before the convention and named Mike Pence on July 15, 2016." Reflects a planning/communication standard about timing and expectations for major convention announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security restrictions and prohibited items
rubrics_metrics.description: Secret Service will not allow guns at the Republican National Convention; local decisions and organizers banned items such as water guns, tennis balls, coolers and lasers in the event zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording includes: "Secret Service: We're not allowing firearms at the Republican National Convention" and references: "Tennis balls, coolers, lasers: What's been banned at the RNC" and "Water guns will be banned at Cleveland's Republican National Convention — firearms won't be." Context: bans and security planning were motivated by concerns about violence and crowd control; these are procedural requirements attendees and protesters had to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech originality and plagiarism expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Melania Trump's speech 'almost immediately came under scrutiny when striking similarities were discovered' with Michelle Obama's 2008 DNC speech; the campaign initially denied allegations, and RNC leaders said if plagiarism were found it would be reasonable to fire the writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: media found similarities; Turnitin analysis reported ~6% overlap and types of plagiarism; Reince Priebus described the speech as 'inspirational' but said 'if plagiarism were found, he thought "it certainly seems reasonable" to fire the person who wrote the speech.' This sets an implicit standard of originality and accountability for convention speeches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention scheduling and nightly themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Convention planners released the official schedule of events and speakers along with themes for each night (e.g., July 18 – 'Make America Safe Again'; July 19 – 'Make America Work Again'; July 20 – 'Make America First Again'; July 21 – 'Make America One Again').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "On July 17, 2016, the convention planners released the convention's official schedule of events and speakers, along with themes." Shows an organizational standard: arranging speakers and content around nightly themes and publishing an official schedule prior to the event.
